GO-01.name: Unchecked error return values
GO-01.description: Errors are assigned to `_` and discarded.

RS-01.name: Nested `RwLock` / `Mutex` acquisition
RS-01.description: Holding multiple locks at once creates deadlock risk.

SEC-01.name: SQL / NoSQL / OS command injection
SEC-01.description: No SQL / NoSQL / OS command injection: use parameterized queries and array argument lists.

TS-01.name: `any` type escape
TS-01.description: Function parameters or return values use `any`.

U-01.name: Respect the requested API contract
U-01.description: Preserve public APIs unless the requested change includes changing them.

W-01.name: No fixes without root cause
W-01.description: No fixes without root cause: reproduce first, then form one hypothesis, then fix.

GO-02.name: Goroutine leak
GO-02.description: `go func()` launches work without an exit path.

PY-02.name: Bare `except` blocks
PY-02.description: `except:` or `except Exception` without logging or re-raising.

RS-02.name: TOCTOU — `get()` followed by `insert()`
RS-02.description: The lock is released between read and write, which creates a race.

SEC-02.name: Hardcoded keys / credentials / API tokens
SEC-02.description: No hardcoded keys, credentials, or API tokens. Load from env / secret manager.

U-02.name: Do not extract abstractions for code that appears only once
U-02.description: Three lines of duplication are better than one premature abstraction.

W-02.name: Back off after 3 consecutive failures
W-02.description: After 3 consecutive failed fixes on the same problem, stop and challenge the hypothesis or architecture.

GO-03.name: Data race
GO-03.description: Shared variables are accessed without a mutex or channel protection.

SEC-03.name: Unescaped user input rendered directly into HTML

TS-03.name: `==` instead of `===`
TS-03.description: Loose equality is used outside explicit null checks.

U-03.name: Do not replace readable duplication with macros
U-03.description: Macros reduce readability and IDE support.

W-03.name: Verify before claiming completion
W-03.description: Verify before claiming completion: produce fresh command output proving the claim.

GO-04.name: Interface is declared on the implementation side instead of the consumer side
GO-04.description: Interface is declared on the implementation side instead of the consumer side

RS-04.name: Multiple `Signal` / `Arc` objects manage the same logical state
RS-04.description: Converge them into a single `Signal<State>` so one structure owns the whole state.

SEC-04.name: API endpoints missing authentication or authorization checks

U-04.name: Do not add features the user did not ask for

W-04.name: Test first
W-04.description: For new features, prefer writing the failing test first, then writing the minimum implementation needed to pass it.

GO-05.name: Repeated error-wrapping patterns across multiple places
GO-05.description: Repeated error-wrapping patterns across multiple places

PY-05.name: Repeated try/except patterns across many locations
PY-05.description: Repeated try/except patterns across many locations

TS-05.name: Repeated fetch / API call patterns across the codebase
TS-05.description: Repeated fetch / API call patterns across the codebase

U-05.name: Do not delete code that merely looks unused without confirming first
U-05.description: It may be a work-in-progress feature.

W-05.name: Sub-agent context isolation
W-05.description: When using sub-agents, give each child only the minimum context required for its task.

RS-06.name: The same match arm is duplicated across multiple methods
RS-06.description: The same match arm is duplicated across multiple methods

SEC-06.name: Weak cryptographic algorithms
SEC-06.description: Using MD5 or SHA1 for password hashing.

TS-06.description: `useEffect` has missing or overly broad dependencies

TS-07.description: Large arrays are mapped during render without memoization

RS-08.name: Unnecessary `clone()` calls
RS-08.description: Often appears on `Copy` types or values that could be borrowed.

TS-08.name: Bypassing type checks with `as any` or `@ts-ignore`
TS-08.description: Bypassing type checks with `as any` or `@ts-ignore`

U-08.name: Do not skip verification steps
U-08.description: See W-03 and W-16 for canonical verification guidance.

U-09.name: Do not bundle unrelated fixes into one commit
U-09.description: Keep commits atomic so they are easy to review and revert.

GO-10.name: Package-level `init()` has side effects
GO-10.description: Network or file I/O happens in `init()`.

SEC-10.name: Logs contain sensitive information
SEC-10.description: Passwords or tokens appear in logs.

U-10.name: Do not guess user intent

PY-11.description: File operations without a `with` context manager

RS-11.description: Logging, config paths, or DB connection strategies drift across modules.

SEC-11.description: AI-generated code carries higher security risk; mandatory human review for auth, payments, secrets, `innerHTML` / `eval` / `exec`.

TS-11.name: Unhandled `null` / `undefined`
TS-11.description: Missing optional chaining or null guards.

PY-12.description: Repeated calls to `len()`, `keys()`, or `values()` inside loops

TS-12.description: Passing full objects as component props instead of only required fields

W-12.description: Protect test integrity: fix production code, never weaken assertions or tamper with test infrastructure.

PY-13.description: A file that only re-exports symbols from another module and adds no behavior should be removed after migration is complete.

TS-13.description: Multiple files define React components or hooks with equivalent behavior but different names.

U-13.description: For example, `SERVER_DB_PATH` and `DESKTOP_DB_PATH` point at different defaults.

W-13.name: Review unproductive exploration
W-13.description: Consecutive Read / Glob / Grep events are an observation, not proof of analysis paralysis.

RS-14.description: Configs, traits, or persistence layers are declared but never integrated into startup.

U-14.description: Different entry points use different base directories.

W-14.description: At most one writable session may operate on a repository; parallel helpers must remain read-only.

U-15.name: Prefer immutability
U-15.description: Create new objects instead of mutating existing ones.

W-15.name: Low-information loop detection
W-15.description: If the information gain shrinks for three consecutive rounds, stop that direction and report it.

SEC-16.description: AI-generated security patches do not have a uniform safety profile.

U-16.name: Keep file size under control
U-16.description: Keep changes localized. The configured size guard blocks new oversized files and growth beyond its limit; existing oversized files may be edited without growth.

W-16.description: Verification commands must come from this session. "Earlier passed" / "should work" do not count.

SEC-17.description: Third-party agent skills are persistent instruction and execution surfaces.

U-17.name: Handle errors completely
U-17.description: Handle errors completely. Do not swallow exceptions silently.

SEC-18.name: External agent input safety requires semantic scoring, not keyword filters alone
SEC-18.description: External content that reaches an agent can be malicious even when it contains no obvious override keywords.

U-18.name: Validate inputs
U-18.description: Validate all user input at system boundaries.

W-18.name: Evaluations must validate path, not only output

U-19.name: Follow the project's data-access boundaries
U-19.description: Use the project's established data-access pattern.

U-20.name: Keep API response shapes consistent
U-20.description: Follow the existing API contract and error conventions.

W-20.name: Long tasks must pin runtime, tools, and rules

U-21.name: Follow the project's commit convention
U-21.description: Explain why the change exists and follow the repository's commit format.

W-21.name: Evidence must be provably executed, not merely cited
W-21.description: Evidence must be provably executed, not merely cited. Verify "decisive" claims through an out-of-session channel before naming a mechanism.

U-22.name: Verify changed behavior
U-22.description: Use the project's coverage policy and meaningful checks for changed behavior; no universal percentage or file-count quota.

U-23.name: No silent degradation
U-23.description: See U-29 for canonical no-silent-degradation guidance.

U-24.name: Keep naming changes within scope
U-24.description: Follow the project's naming and compatibility policy.

U-25.name: Fix build failures first
U-25.description: Fix build failures first before any other edit; do not add new code while build is red.

U-26.description: Declaration-execution completeness: declared Config / Trait / persistence layers must be wired into startup.

U-29.name: Error-driven downgrade paths must be observable at error level
U-29.description: No silent degradation: errors causing user-visible missing data or wrong output must `error` or raise, not `warning` + fallback.

W-30.description: Agent harness evaluation must audit the trajectory, not only final task completion.

U-31.name: Cache keys must include code version
U-31.description: When builder or generation logic changes, old cache entries must invalidate automatically.

U-32.name: Review instruction overload
U-32.description: Treat instruction counts as a file-based estimate, not proof of runtime loading, semantic conflict, or task failure.

U-33.name: Code search defaults to glob/grep; large codebases require structural navigation
U-33.description: For agent code retrieval, plain glob/grep driven by the model remains the default for small and medium single-repository work.

W-37.description: An agent memory or experience layer that feeds future inference must learn from both successful and failed trajectories.

W-38.name: Tool-need recognition and tool-call execution are separate metrics
W-38.description: Tool-use evals must distinguish whether an agent recognized that a tool was needed from whether it actually called the tool.

W-42.description: Agent workflows that repeatedly modify and hand off the same artifact must measure semantic fidelity at fixed checkpoints.

TASTE-ANSI.name: Hardcoded ANSI escape sequences
TASTE-ANSI.description: Use a crate like `colored` or `termcolor` instead of hardcoding `\x1b[` sequences.
